summary: NASA left iconic scientific equipment across the solar system, but students often dismiss these historical instruments as inert "space junk." AFTERSIGNAL: Echoes of the Forgotten Moon bridges this gap through interactive storytelling. Players guide PIP, an autonomous archival robot, across Apollo 15’s reconstructed Hadley–Apennine landing site. By tracing power cables, toggling "Echo Vision" to reveal historical astronaut tracks, and opening hands-on workstations, players analyze authentic 1972 NASA moonquake recordings, investigate heat-flow probe depths, and simulate lunar laser ranging. The experience proves our core message to the next generation of explorers: the instruments fell silent, but their discoveries didn't.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

AFTERSIGNAL: Echoes of the Forgotten Moon is an atmospheric 2.5D exploration adventure and scientific mystery game set in a digital reconstruction of NASA’s Apollo 15 landing site at Hadley–Apennine. Players control PIP, a small archival exploration robot, to investigate silent lunar equipment.

Rather than moving through a linear corridor, players explore an interconnected lunar hub, following historical power and data cables branching from the SNAP-27 nuclear generator to individual experiments. Players use "Echo Vision" (V key) to toggle between the silent present and an active archival reconstruction that illuminates surface conduits and astronaut EVA tracks. At each instrument, players open interactive workstations:

  1. The Seismometer (PSE): Zoom into authentic NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) recordings of a 13 May 1972 meteoroid strike, identify P-wave and S-wave arrivals, compare travel times across Apollo stations, and sonify the 2-hour lunar ringing coda.
  2. The Heat Flow Probes (HFE): Examine real borehole depths (162 cm162\text{ cm}162 cm vs. 160 cm160\text{ cm}160 cm) to see how deep probes bypass day–night temperature swings, unlocking the 2018 discovery that astronaut footprints darkened the soil and warmed the regolith.
  3. The Retroreflector (LRRR): Aim an Earth observatory laser at a 300 corner-cube silica array, simulating 90° total internal reflection, measuring the 2.56-second photon round-trip time, and discovering the Moon’s +3.8 cm/year+3.8\text{ cm/year}+3.8 cm/year orbital drift.

Every discovery populates The Last Field Report Evidence Board (Tab key), answering five core questions for each machine (Identity, Purpose, Mechanism, Discovery, Legacy) before transmitting the completed archive back to Earth.

What benefits does it have?

  • Active Scientific Inquiry over Passive Reading: Instead of reading abstract textbook sentences like "the Moon rang like a bell", students actively measure the waveform and hear the audio sonification of fractured lunar crust vibrating.
  • Direct Primary-Source Engagement: Demystifies raw planetary science archives by putting real NASA data directly into learners' hands in an intuitive, visual format.
  • Intergenerational STEM Connection: Bridges Apollo-era engineering to modern lunar exploration (such as the Artemis program) by demonstrating how past measurements continue to shape future missions.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is to dismantle the widespread myth that abandoned space hardware is merely "space junk." By engaging middle- and high-school students (ages 10–18) and educators through interactive storytelling, AFTERSIGNAL shows that these instruments formed humanity’s first extraterrestrial geophysical observatories. The project inspires curiosity in planetary geophysics, physics, and aerospace engineering by proving that historical scientific records continue to yield major breakthroughs decades after missions conclude.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Game Engine: Phaser 4 running Arcade Physics with low-gravity kinematics (g=720 px/s2g = 720\text{ px/s}^2g=720 px/s2).
  • Languages & Build Tools: TypeScript (strict type safety) and Vite (ESM bundling and production tree-shaking).
  • Audio Architecture: Procedural Web Audio API for real-time synthesizer nodes, biquad filters, and acoustic seismic sonification (zero external audio files).
  • Graphics Generation: 100% procedural HTML5 Canvas 2D vector drawing for terrain, vehicles, and backdrops (zero external image downloads).
  • Data Processing: Python standard library (tools/process_pse.py) to parse, filter, and normalize raw NASA PDS GeoCSV waveform data.
  • Typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible, Michroma, and IBM Plex fonts via open-source web font packages.
  • Deployment: Static web hosting via GitHub Pages.

How is your project creative?

  • Dual-Layer "Echo Vision" Mechanic: Merges past and present into a tactile gameplay loop, letting players visualize invisible radio signals, power ribbons, and historical footprints beneath the lunar dust.
  • Forensic Evidence Board: Replaces generic game scores and arcade collectibles with an investigative synthesis board grounded in real historical questions.
  • PIP's Inner Voice: PIP communicates through subtle, curious robotic monologue subtitles, evoking emotional empathy and scientific wonder without heavy exposition or cutscenes.
  • Acoustic Sonification: Converts seismic motion into audible sound, allowing players to experience planetary physics through their ears.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Scientific & Historical Accuracy: We adhered strictly to verified NASA sources (NASA Planetary Data System, NSSDCA catalogs, and Apollo 15 Preliminary Science Reports). We explicitly maintained the distinction between powered ALSEP instruments (shut down in 1977) and the passive Laser Ranging Retroreflector (still active today).
  • Universal Classroom Accessibility: To ensure students on low-power school Chromebooks or tablets can play without barriers, we built a zero-binary web application that loads in under one second. The UI includes high-contrast text, dyslexia-friendly fonts, keyboard navigation, and screen-reader landmark support.
  • Clear Epistemic Separation: All information in the game carries clear tags (HISTORICAL, SCIENCE, DATA, STORY, GAMEPLAY) so players always know where fictional narrative framing ends and authentic empirical science begins.
  • Multi-World Scalability: We framed the Apollo 15 experience as Chapter 1, establishing an in-game roadmap connecting lunar discoveries to silent Mars sentinels (InSight, Opportunity, Ingenuity) for future expansion.
